clue.text: Torment an animal

definitions.meaning: to torment is to pester or harass someone persistently
a burrowing black-and-white mammal of British woods

explanation.surface: Someone is cruel to a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone relentlessly is to hound them, and the same word names a nocturnal burrowing mammal.

clue.text: To the French head of department it's a full examination

parts.note: au is French for to the

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the apostrophe s is a link, leaving the word it

explanation.surface: A French department head is given a thorough inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is a thorough official inspection of accounts.

clue.text: Undeveloped territory in the island

parts.note: green means immature or unripe
land is territory

explanation.surface: Wild unspoilt country on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's largest island lies between the Arctic and Atlantic Oceans.

clue.text: Spinning club

explanation.surface: A gym's cycling class.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating motion is one sense; the international service organisation is the other.

clue.text: A stirring piece of music

definitions.meaning: a stirring is a motion or shift
a section of a symphony or sonata

explanation.surface: A rousing composition is being praised.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion or shift is one sense; a self-contained section of a symphony is the other.

clue.text: City's race marker befuddled but happy

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A city's racecourse official is confused but cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverbial phrase meaning very cheerful, likening someone to a chirping insect.

clue.text: Tobacco girl

definitions.meaning: a type of tobacco grown originally in the US state

explanation.surface: A girl who smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of tobacco named after a US state, and a female first name.

clue.text: The builder has two relations

parts.note: ma is mother, a relation
a son is a relation

explanation.surface: The construction worker has two relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a builder in stone.

clue.text: Points written by spy who keeps us up to date with events

definitions.text: who keeps us up to date with events

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the compass points
an agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Points made by a secret agent who keeps us informed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a newsagent sells the papers that keep us up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling newspapers provides the latest reports.

clue.text: Speculator coming to the City with some hesitation

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A risk-taking investor arrives in the financial district, a little unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' suggests London's financial district, fitting a speculator, but here it is the ancient city UR.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the word is a person who takes financial risks in a venture, a speculator.

clue.text: Partners have opponents stitched up

indicators.note: one pair of letters holds the other pair, as a container has something within

parts.note: in bridge North and South play as partners
East and West are the partnership opposing North-South at bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge pair complain their opponents cheated them.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners against East and West, so 'Partners' and 'opponents' are pairs of compass letters; 'have' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stitched up has been joined with needle and thread.

clue.text: A stringy sort of fish

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so these letters are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Describing some fish as stringy in texture.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous barbed tail is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Ancient Greek island occupied by one nymph originally

indicators.note: the island's name is taken over by the letter for one, which sits within it

parts.note: Iona is a small island in the Hebrides
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word nymph is taken

explanation.surface: An island in Greece was once home to a single nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA, the Hebridean island, takes I inside to give IONIA, then N from the start of 'nymph'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionians were one of the main peoples of ancient Greece, settled around the Aegean.

clue.text: Silver god found in India

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A silver idol is discovered in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of the Taj Mahal lies in Uttar Pradesh, northern India.

clue.text: A cooked meat in Gaul? Perhaps in the country

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are messed about, as when the books are cooked

explanation.surface: A meat dish in France, perhaps out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American republic is a country.

clue.text: Insulted an insignificant journalist

parts.note: slight means trivial or small
ED is short for editor, a newspaper journalist

explanation.surface: A minor reporter was rudely snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be snubbed or treated with disrespect is to be insulted.

clue.text: Obstacle encountered as rustic hurried to church

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
ran means hurried
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A farmhand dashing to church meets an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impedes is an obstacle.

clue.text: One Name certain about City being dodgy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for certain goes round the city's postcode

parts.note: sure means certain
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: One name is sure about a city being shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means unsafe or precarious, near to dodgy.

clue.text: Cynical, in a way, during a kind of boom

indicators.note: the words a way come in the middle of the boom, as something happening during it

parts.note: a sonic boom is made by an aircraft breaking the sound barrier
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone is scornful, after a fashion, while a jet goes supersonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' looks like a qualifier on 'Cynical', but 'in' is only a link; 'during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and scornfully cynical are near synonyms.

clue.text: The head's out of his mind

definitions.meaning: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: The headteacher has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the head plus 's, and slang for crazy.

clue.text: A refusal by Sir John's crony? Just the opposite

parts.note: no is a refusal
Nym is a follower of Sir John Falstaff in Shakespeare's history plays

explanation.surface: Falstaff's friend refuses something, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Nym sounds like a name (Greek onyma); the answer means no name, just the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameless person or pseudonym is the opposite of a named one.

clue.text: Archbishop takes the lawyers' place

definitions.meaning: William and Frederick ... were both Archbishops of Canterbury
the Inner and Middle ... are London Inns of Court where barristers have chambers

explanation.surface: A senior churchman moves into the legal quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Temple is a district of central London housing two Inns of Court, the barristers' societies.
explanation.definitionFit: Two archbishops of Canterbury bore this surname, and a London Inns of Court district bears the same name.

clue.text: It beats having beans, for instance

definitions.meaning: the heart's throb at the wrist
edible seeds of legumes such as lentils and peas

explanation.surface: Something is better than having beans.
explanation.definitionFit: The throb of blood in arteries, and the edible seeds of legumes.

clue.text: No rating could be so unenlightened…

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: A sailor with no rank must be badly informed.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor, which steers the surface to the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or education is being unenlightened.

clue.text: Originally not allowing such awful language in this passage

indicators.note: the original letters of each word, taken in turn

explanation.surface: Forbidding foul language in this piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests text, but it is the nasal passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal describes the nose, a passage for air.

clue.text: …as to let the boat deviate to port

parts.note: a ship that yaws swings off course
L stands for left, which is port at sea

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: an ignorant sailor lets the vessel drift left.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the clue before; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel is a type of boat.

clue.text: "And his — may defeat my life" (Othello)

parts.note: Desdemona's line in Othello Act 4, with the missing word for cruelty filling the blank

explanation.surface: A line from Othello with a gap to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: The word missing from Desdemona's line means cruelty or harshness.

clue.text: Action intended, say, by an Irish nationalist

parts.note: a legal action is a case

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken, giving letters that sound like it

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Legal proceedings planned by an Irish patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Casement was an Irish nationalist executed in 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Roger Casement was a campaigner for Irish independence, hanged for treason in 1916.

clue.text: One mule's possibly had it for breakfast

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter beyond the word mules
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single mule has eaten something for its morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit is a common morning dish.
